statement_summary: One program aligned to CSF 2.0; OT standard based on SP 800-82 Rev. 3; NERC CIP program for the Electric Utility
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R1); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)

statement_summary: Group CISO accountable; CIP Senior Manager named and delegations documented; division OT security owners named
Annual SP 800-30 risk analysis per division with roll-up to group
Risk acceptance authority by level; safety Highs and potential NERC noncompliance cannot be accepted
Division supplements may not weaken group policy; re-align within 90 days; annual attestation
Common control catalog; each division documents inheritance per system
Sanctions for policy violations
Vendors and affiliates need contract security terms and an assessment before OT, CEII, or BCSI access; an affiliate serving another division is a vendor
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2, R2); client contracts

statement_summary: Independent annual assessment of common controls with division samples
Exceptions written, risk-rated, approved, 12 months maximum; none may create a potential CIP noncompliance
Retention: security records 6 years; CIP evidence at least three calendar years
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP standards, Compliance section 1.2 evidence retention)

statement_summary: AI systems registered and approved under the Group AI Standard
Potential NERC noncompliance reported within 2 business days; CIP Senior Manager decides self-reports
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (NERC Rules of Procedure Appendix 4C self-reports)

statement_summary: Unique identities; shared accounts only for documented device limits
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-007-6 R5 Part 5.3 for TCC); N21-BM (CSF PR.AA-01)

statement_summary: Role-based least privilege; BCSI, CEII, and client BCSI only through authorized access lists
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-004-7 R4, R6); client CIP-011-3 terms

statement_summary: MFA for all IT access and all remote OT access; phishing-resistant for administrators
OT remote access only through SYS-G4 or the TCC Intermediate System; per-session approval; no standing vendor or affiliate access; malicious-communication detection
No account reaches more than one division OT environment without each owner's approval
Disable access within 4 hours of termination; contractor accounts expire; client notices of departures
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-004-7 R5); client CIP-013-2 Part 1.2.3 terms

statement_summary: Quarterly access certification; inactive accounts disabled after 45 days
Just-in-time privileged IT access; tiered OT administrator rights
Lockout and session lock; operator consoles alarm instead of locking
Break-glass accounts tested quarterly
Two-person rule for switching orders and bulk AMI disconnects
Physical access to control centers, substations, the POC, and server rooms authorized, reviewed, and logged
Report suspected incidents immediately to the SOC and, in OT, the shift supervisor
One severity scale; any OT effect or multi-division incident is Severity 1
Safety first: shift supervisor decides containment steps that affect operations
Record occurrence, identification, and determination times for each reporting clock
Reporting duties follow the notification matrix (CIP-008-6, DOE-417, EOP-004-4, client contracts, FAR, state laws)
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-008-6 R4; CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 4); EOP-004-4 R2; DOE-417; FAR 52.204-25(d); state breach laws

statement_summary: Disclosure committee within 24 hours of Severity 1; Form 8-K Item 1.05 within 4 business days of a materiality determination
No ransom payment without board, counsel, insurer, and OFAC sanctions check
Testing: annual division tests; CIP-008-6 and CIP-009-6 every 15 months; low impact plan every 36 months; annual cross-division tabletop
Preserve evidence with chain of custody without delaying recovery
Lessons learned within 30 days; CIP plan updates within the CIP-008-6 R3 and CIP-009-6 R3 times
Recover in BIA order; OT remote access last
Owner and classification for every data set; highest level applies
Encrypt Restricted and Confidential data in transit and at rest
regulatory_driver: State breach laws (Fla. Stat. 501.171 worked example); client contracts

statement_summary: Designated BCSI storage locations, including vendor and affiliate locations, with verified access lists
Client CEII and BCSI only in restricted folders with client-approved access lists; FERC CEII only with written authorization
Federal Contract Information under FAR 52.204-21 controls
Minimize personal information; no SSNs after credit decisions; secure royalty transfers
No Restricted or client data in personal storage or unapproved services, including AI tools
Sanitize or destroy media with certificates; BCSI before reuse or disposal
Only company-managed devices on OT and client substations; Transient Cyber Asset rules before each connection
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-010-4 R4; CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 5); client terms

statement_summary: Scan removable media at an approved kiosk before OT use
No company or client information in personal storage or devices
Approved AI tools only, with approved data classes; client consent for client data; engineer review of AI-assisted work
regulatory_driver: Group AI Standard; client confidentiality terms

statement_summary: Report phishing and suspected incidents
